about: Mr. Krabs Blur is a heavily smeared, low-quality frame of Mr. Krabs from SpongeBob SquarePants, his mouth stretched open in a scream and his whole body streaked with motion blur, while a green fish customer behind him is just as distorted. Everything looks like it is shaking. The image reads as pure panic or sensory overload, the feeling of your brain rattling inside your skull. People use it for frantic moments: realising a deadline is today, hearing your name called unexpectedly, or a wild plot twist.
usage:
The top box sets up the moment, usually starting with "me when" or "me after". The bottom box finishes it with the trigger: the shocking news, the loud noise or the sheer chaos that sent Mr. Krabs into a blur.

The blur already conveys the reaction, so spend your words on making the situation specific and relatable. Sudden realisations, overstimulation and caffeine-fuelled meltdowns all fit. The template also works split across both boxes as one sentence, which keeps each line short enough to read over the blurry picture.
